label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 6
knowledgePattern: Find a radical equation’s full feasible parameter set before testing sufficiency
solution:
The equation asks where the increasing left-hand curve meets the horizontal line at the parameter height.

The left side is nonnegative, so k≥0. When k≥0, both radical domains together require x≥k. For fixed k, the left side is continuous and strictly increasing in x, has minimum 2k at x=k, and grows without bound.

Therefore a solution exists precisely when k≥2k. The case k=0 works at x=0. For k>0, squaring gives k2≥2k, hence k≥2.

The complete successful set is k = 0 or k ≥ 2. Option A lies entirely inside it. B and D include k = 1; C includes k = 3/2; E includes k = 1, all of which fail. Answer A.

hints.title: Check which values are allowed
hints.body: Square roots and fourth roots cannot be negative. What does that tell you about k? Also require both expressions inside the roots to be nonnegative.
hints.recap: Square roots need a nonnegative input. A fourth root means taking the square root twice.
hints.pitfall: Both roots must exist at the same value of x.
hints.pause: Write the restrictions on k and x; check k = 0 separately.

recall.reminder: Square roots need a nonnegative input. A fourth root means taking the square root twice.

hints.title: Find the smallest left-hand side
hints.body: Keep the parameter fixed. Sketch the increasing left-hand side from its smallest allowed input and calculate its starting height. Draw the horizontal target level: when can the two meet?
hints.recap: Square roots increase as their inputs increase; taking another square root keeps that order.
hints.pitfall: Check the endpoint rather than guessing where a graph starts.
hints.pause: Decide when the left-hand side can reach the height k.

recall.reminder: Square roots increase as their inputs increase; taking another square root keeps that order.

hints.title: Check every value allowed by an option
hints.body: Use your condition for a solution to test each option. A sufficient condition must work for every value of k that it allows.
hints.recap: Sufficient means that the condition guarantees a solution.
hints.pitfall: It may leave out other values of k that would also work.
hints.pause: Reject an option if you can find one value it allows that fails.
